q.t: A fair coin is tossed. What is the probability of a tail?
q.e: Two equally likely outcomes, one of them a tail.

q.t: A die is thrown. What is the probability of a 6?
q.e: One favourable face out of six equally likely faces.

q.t: What is the probability of a sure (certain) event?
q.e: Every outcome is favourable: favourable ÷ total = 1.

q.t: A die is thrown. What is the probability of an odd number?
q.e: 1, 3 and 5 — three of the six faces.

q.t: Two coins are tossed together. How many outcomes are possible?
q.e: HH, HT, TH, TT. Each coin has 2 outcomes: 2 × 2.

q.t: A bag has 4 red and 6 blue balls. What is the probability of drawing a red ball?
q.e: 4 red out of 10 balls = 2/5.

q.t: What is the probability of an impossible event?
q.e: No outcome is favourable.

q.t: A letter is chosen at random from the word APPLE. What is the probability that it is P?
q.e: 5 letters, 2 of them P.

q.t: Cards numbered 1 to 10 are shuffled. What is the probability of drawing an even number?
q.e: 2, 4, 6, 8, 10 — five of the ten cards.

q.t: A probability can never be:
q.e: Favourable outcomes can never outnumber all the outcomes.

q.t: A die is thrown. What is the probability of a multiple of 3?
q.e: 3 and 6 — two of six faces.

q.t: A die is thrown. What is the probability of NOT getting a 5?
q.e: Five of the six faces are not 5. (Or 1 − 1/6.)

q.t: One card is drawn from a pack of 52. What is the probability that it is a king?
q.e: There are 4 kings: 4/52 = 1/13.

q.t: One card is drawn from a pack of 52. What is the probability that it is red?
q.e: Hearts and diamonds are red: 26 of the 52 cards.

q.t: One card is drawn from a pack of 52. What is the probability that it is a heart?
q.e: 13 hearts out of 52 = 1/4 (one of four suits).

q.t: A bag has 5 white, 7 black and 3 red balls. What is the probability of drawing a ball that is NOT black?
q.e: White + red = 8 out of 15.

q.t: A number is chosen at random from 1 to 20. What is the probability that it is prime?
q.k: F(len([n for n in range(2,21) if all(n%d for d in range(2,n))]),20)

q.t: A spinner has 5 equal sectors, 2 of them red. What is the probability of landing on red?
q.e: 2 red sectors out of 5 equal ones.

q.t: A lottery sells 1000 tickets and has 5 prizes. What is the probability that one ticket wins a prize?
The probability of an event is 0.3. What is the probability that it does not happen?
q.e: P(E) + P(not E) = 1.

q.t: Two coins are tossed. What is the probability of two heads?
q.e: Only HH out of HH, HT, TH, TT.

q.t: Two coins are tossed. What is the probability of at least one tail?
q.e: HT, TH and TT — three of four. (Or 1 − P(HH).)

q.t: One card is drawn from a pack of 52. What is the probability that it is a face card (jack, queen or king)?
q.e: 3 face cards in each of 4 suits = 12. 12/52 = 3/13.

q.t: One card is drawn from a pack of 52. What is the probability that it is a red king?
q.e: The kings of hearts and diamonds: 2/52 = 1/26.

q.t: Two dice are thrown. What is the probability that the numbers add up to 10?
q.k: F(len([1 for a in range(1,7) for b in range(1,7) if a+b==10]),36)

q.t: A number is chosen at random from 1 to 50. What is the probability that it is a multiple of 6?
q.k: F(len([n for n in range(1,51) if n%6==0]),50)

q.t: A bag has 3 red, 5 blue and some green balls. The probability of drawing a green ball is 1/3. How many green balls are there?
q.k: [x for x in range(1,50) if F(x,8+x)==F(1,3)][0]

q.t: Of 200 families with two children, 64 have 2 girls, 96 have 1 girl and 40 have no girls. What is the probability that a family chosen at random has exactly 1 girl?
q.e: 96/200 = 12/25, based on the survey results.

q.t: One card is drawn from a pack of 52. What is the probability that it is NOT an ace?
q.e: 48 of the 52 cards are not aces: 48/52 = 12/13.

q.t: One card is drawn from a pack of 52. What is the probability that it is the ace of spades?
q.e: There is exactly one such card.

q.t: Two dice are thrown. What is the probability that the sum is 10 or more?
q.k: F(len([1 for a in range(1,7) for b in range(1,7) if a+b>=10]),36)

q.t: Two dice are thrown. What is the probability that the product of the numbers is odd?
q.k: F(len([1 for a in range(1,7) for b in range(1,7) if a*b%2==1]),36)
q.e: A product is odd only when BOTH numbers are odd: 3 × 3 = 9 of the 36 outcomes.

q.t: Two dice are thrown. What is the probability that the sum is a prime number?
q.k: F(len([1 for a in range(1,7) for b in range(1,7) if a+b in (2,3,5,7,11)]),36)

q.t: Three coins are tossed. What is the probability of exactly two heads?
q.e: HHT, HTH, THH — three of the 8 outcomes.

q.t: Three coins are tossed. What is the probability of at least two heads?
q.e: Exactly two (3 ways) or all three (1 way): 4/8 = 1/2.

q.t: What is the probability that a leap year chosen at random has 53 Sundays?
q.e: 366 days = 52 weeks + 2 extra days. The extra pair can be any of 7 pairs, and 2 of them include a Sunday.

q.t: One king is lost from a pack of 52 cards. A card is drawn from the rest. What is the probability that it is a king?
q.e: 51 cards remain, 3 of them kings: 3/51 = 1/17.

q.t: A number is chosen at random from 1 to 100. What is the probability that it is a perfect square?
q.e: 1², 2², … 10² — ten squares.

q.t: A two-digit number is chosen at random. What is the probability that both its digits are the same?
q.e: There are 90 two-digit numbers (10 to 99), and 11, 22, … 99 are 9 of them.

q.t: A bag has 12 balls, some of them white. When 6 more white balls are added, the probability of drawing a white ball doubles. How many white balls were there at first?
q.k: [x for x in range(1,12) if F(x+6,18)==2*F(x,12)][0]
